I'll work through each chapter draft systematically, applying the gate test to every potential seam.

---

**Ch 011 draft — the hallway/badger scene compression**

The source has Miriam use the sheet-ambush (authorized cut), then flee into the hallway, then choose the side door. The draft compresses this to:

> "I rapped the wood and shouted, 'Help! Somebody help! There's a-um, a badger in here!' Great one, heroine. I got nothing useful back but the cold. All right—if the main way out was locked, then through the side door to anywhere but here."

The badger cry is an authorized cut residue (the badger ruse IS the authorized cut). But the sentence "I got nothing useful back but the cold" is a seam left by that cut — the source had the badger shout *work* (servants came, she ambushed them with the sheet). In the draft, the shout apparently fails, and she pivots to the side door. That pivot is internally coherent in the draft: she tries the front door, it's locked, she shouts, nothing works, she tries the side door. A reader follows this logic without confusion. This is an authorized-cut residue, not a finding.

---

**Ch 011 draft — entry into the lord's room**

The source establishes she enters via the side door (which connects her room to his) *after* the sheet ambush forces her into the hall and she ducks into the last door on the passage — which turns out to be his room via the side door. In the draft the path is: front door locked → shout fails → side door. The side door leads directly to his room. This is compressed but parseable.

---

**Ch 011 — "She is found and that is all that needs be done on your part"**

In the source, this makes sense: the lord knows via the mark where she is (under his bed), so he's telling the staff she's been located. In the draft the same line appears. Has the reader been told about the mark yet at this point in the dialogue? No — the mark revelation comes *after* the staff leaves. So the lord's line "She is found" is slightly mysterious to the reader until the next paragraph — but this is the same in the source. Not a finding; the mystery is intentional and resolves immediately.

---

**Ch 011 — "How and when?" then "Only a moment ago."**

Source has: "Only a moment ago, and she-well, she threw a blanket over my husband and me." The draft cuts the blanket-over-husband detail (authorized cut residue). The truncated reply "Only a moment ago" still parses. Not a finding.

---

**Ch 011 — the old woman's husband**

The source establishes the old woman's husband is one of the servants she tripped over. The draft never introduces the husband at all (authorized cut). When the old woman says "I'm sorry your assistance was needed, my lord" — this line survives in the draft and refers to no established prior event, but it's a residue of the authorized cut. Not a finding.

---

**Ch 011 — "I'm not—" interrupted**

> "I cringed and clung to the boards. 'I'm not—'"

This is a fragment, but it's clearly an interrupted speech (em-dash), immediately followed by the lord cutting her off with his next line. Parseable as interrupted dialogue. Not a finding.

---

After careful examination of both chapters, I find no structurally damaging compressions that pass the gate test and fall outside authorized cuts.
